Package dev.gmitch215.bytebox.locks

Class ReentrantLock

java.lang.Object
dev.gmitch215.bytebox.locks.ReentrantLock
public class ReentrantLock extends Object
java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock, which the class library does not carry at all.

This lock never waits. One fiber runs at a time, so an uncontended acquire is already exclusive and needs nothing to make it so. Contention has exactly one cause here: a fiber suspended while holding the lock and a second fiber reached the same critical section. That case is refused rather than approximated, because the alternative is letting two fibers into a section written on the assumption that one enters.

Blocking until the owner leaves would be the faithful answer, and it is not available: a substituted class cannot contain a suspending call, and Object.wait is one. So the choice is between refusing contention and ignoring it, and a library that guards a cache with a lock never reaches either branch.

Since:
1.0.2
